title: JPMorgan's On-the-Ground Research: The 'Monetization Moment' for China's AI Has Arrived, with Workflows Outpacing Base Models
summary: The investment logic in China's AI sector is quietly shifting—model rankings are no longer the core focus, and who controls customer data, workflow access points, and pricing power has become critical. JPMorgan's latest research shows that vertical scenarios with heavy processes and rich data, such as insurance risk control, enterprise data integration, and cross-border marketing, are first to demonstrate commercial value; computing power and infrastructure have become the most certain main line due to increasing model substitutability; consumer-level AI still lacks a solid revenue proof.
content:
The investment logic in China's AI industry is undergoing a subtle shift: markets previously focused on model capabilities, parameters, and rankings, but now should pay more attention to who controls customer data, workflow access points, deployment capabilities, and pricing power. Eight meetings covering autonomous driving, independent model development, enterprise workflow software, and vertical AI applications have provided a common signal: models remain important, but in some enterprise scenarios, models are beginning to act like replaceable input items.

According to market observers, JPMorgan Securities (China) analysts Yao Cheng and others stated in their May 22 report on the Chinese AI industry that "some AI applications are showing early signs of commercial value, particularly in vertical areas with intensive workflows and abundant data." The key point of this statement is not that AI applications finally can generate revenue, but rather where this revenue begins to emerge: not in general chat or simple API calls, but in scenarios such as insurance and financial risk, enterprise data integration, and cross-border marketing, which are process-heavy, data-rich, and result-measurable.

This also changes some assumptions about autonomous driving and application layers. Previously, a more conservative framework was: "Robotaxi is more of a cost center in the short term, and AI application monetization is still early; the clearest public market exposure lies in infrastructure and computing power." Now, ADAS is closer to mass production and scaling, and there are claims of city-level economic improvements in some L4 autonomous driving deployments. Vertical AI applications are also beginning to show early evidence of recurring revenue, value-based pricing, and operational profitability. However, these evidences mostly come from management statements, and many companies are not yet publicly listed, so they are still far from auditable and replicable public market validation.

The investment implications have become more concentrated: computing power, AI infrastructure, domestic chips, memory, and storage are the least risky directions that do not require betting on the success of a single large model. For the application layer, look at proprietary data, workflow ownership, customer retention, and pricing power; model companies must prove they are not just being called upon, but can control high-value workflows. Consumer-level AI and intelligent e-commerce have not yet provided sufficient hard evidence of payment, retention, and transaction growth, and valuation stories still need to be discounted.

Model capabilities remain important, but the moat of pure API selling is thinning

The most consistent signal comes from enterprise scenarios: customers care about whether tasks can be completed, whether they can be embedded into existing processes, and whether they can leverage their own data, rather than necessarily using the largest model.

Some companies are already allocating requests to different domestic models and cutting-edge models based on price, performance, and specific tasks. Some companies have admitted that the switching cost of pure APIs is not high, and what truly keeps customers is enterprise data integration, workflow transformation, and post-deployment business stickiness.

This is uncomfortable for model layer valuations. Usage growth can continue to exist, but whether the rent stays with model vendors becomes another issue. If customers can switch models with low friction, the pricing pressure of general APIs will become increasingly obvious.

Of course, models are not without value. In tasks such as coding, intelligent agents, and enterprise software automation, reliability, context length, tool calling ability, and multi-step task completion rate directly affect business outcomes. If model companies can control user interfaces, workflow memory, and data feedback loops, they still have the opportunity to retain economic value in high-value scenarios.

The earliest monetizable applications are not general AI, but vertical scenarios with heavy processes and rich data

Insurance and financial services risk, enterprise data integration, and cross-border marketing are the strongest signals in this round. Their commonality is clear: customers pay not because they "used AI," but because of reduced risk, improved efficiency, better marketing conversion, and automated decision-making.

These scenarios are easier to value. As long as results are measurable, suppliers have the opportunity to convert AI capabilities into recurring revenue, rather than one-time project fees.

However, it is not possible to directly apply traditional software valuation logic. Some businesses may still have strong service attributes: high concentration of major clients, small share in the client's wallet, and early deployment requiring significant manual implementation or assistance. If these costs are fully accounted for, gross margins and scalability may not appear as good as they seem.

Therefore, a more accurate judgment is: some AI applications have moved from narrative to early commercial validation, but have not yet proven they possess sustainable, scalable software economics.

The computing power mainline is actually clearer: the more replaceable the model, the more infrastructure becomes a common winner

If enterprises use multiple models, the exclusivity of models will decrease, but the demand for computing power, storage, memory, cloud orchestration, and inference infrastructure will not disappear.

This is where the infrastructure logic becomes clearer. Regardless of which model eventually leads, training, inference, enterprise deployment, ADAS development, simulation, data processing, and managed services all consume computing resources. Model competition may even increase the frequency of experiments and deployments, thereby driving up inference and supporting infrastructure demand.

The key assumption is task volume elasticity. An optimistic scenario requires AI task volume growth to outpace the decline in per-task costs. If model efficiency, sparse computing, edge inference, or architectural improvements cause unit computing power consumption to drop faster, the benefits to infrastructure could be weakened.

Currently, this framework leans more towards the former: demand is expanding from cutting-edge training to inference, domestic technology stack adaptation, memory, storage, and enterprise workflow execution. For the public market, this remains the clearest AI exposure.

Autonomous driving is no longer just a cost center, but L4 is not yet ready

The change in autonomous driving lies in the fact that the previous narrative of pure money burning is starting to loosen.

ADAS and L4 Robotaxi should be viewed separately. ADAS, relying on vehicle manufacturers' mass production, real road data cycles, and software-style bulk profit potential, is closer to scaling. Suppliers can follow car manufacturers' adoption rates to form more visible revenue contributions.

L4 Robotaxi is still much earlier. Some operators have claimed improvements in city-level economics, lower vehicle costs, and better economic viability for overseas deployment, but company-level profitability remains a later goal, and regulatory thresholds have not disappeared. Successfully operating in one city does not mean it can be replicated across different geographies, weather conditions, and regulatory environments.

For L4 companies, the evidence that can truly change investment feasibility is very specific: city-level audit-able unit economics, license expansion to new cities, continuous reduction in vehicle costs, safety records, and regulatory continuity. Any accident that triggers a license suspension could push the commercialization process back by several quarters.

Neutral professional companies can enter carmakers and enterprises, but platforms may not dominate the application layer

Platforms originally had cloud, traffic, ecosystems, and distribution interfaces, and appeared to be able to capture most of the value of AI applications. However, neutrality is becoming a variable in enterprise and automotive procurement.

Some non-platform models or application companies are able to enter整车厂 (vehicle manufacturers) and enterprise orders not because they have a larger ecosystem, but because customers view them as more customizable and neutral suppliers. Platform clouds, maps, and infrastructure can still be used as input layers, but deployment contexts and customer workflows may be controlled by neutral professional companies.

This does not weaken the logic of platforms like Tencent and Alibaba benefiting from cloud, maps, computing, and data infrastructure. What needs to be clearly distinguished is: when platforms act as infrastructure suppliers, and when they take orders in the application layer, these are two separate things.

When customers prioritize neutrality, customization, and deep integration, platform models may not have an inherent advantage. Procurement decisions will depend more on trust, integration depth, and vertical delivery capabilities.

Consumer-level AI and intelligent e-commerce still lack a solid revenue proof

Current evidence for consumer-level AI is weak. Common issues include low user loyalty, fierce competition, insufficient willingness to pay, and rapid product imitation.

Intelligent e-commerce and AI advertising are also in an earlier stage. In cross-border marketing, current optimization is mainly driven by recommendation algorithms, and large language model-driven intelligent agent commercialization has not yet provided sufficient verifiable revenue evidence.

What needs to be observed here is not download numbers, product launches, or demonstration effects, but retention rates, payment conversion rates, repeat usage rates, gross margins, and measurable transaction increments. Without these metrics, the story of consumer-level AI will struggle to support higher valuations.

The real test is retention, pricing, and gross margin, not the AI narrative itself

For model companies, the key question over the next few quarters is: after customers route through multiple models, can the model layer continue to capture value? An optimistic scenario requires seeing rising net retention, stable or improving pricing, low churn, and stable gross margins in the face of multi-model competition.

Coding may be the clearest test scenario. It is frequent, its value is quantifiable, and it has potential for developer interface lock-in. Model-leading entities like Zhipu and MiniMax cannot rely solely on benchmark test performance, but must also prove vertical scenario capabilities, workflow control, and repeatable usage quality.

For application companies, the key metrics are revenue quality, customer concentration, implementation intensity, net retention, pricing structure, and true gross margin after deducting customer support and manual assistance.

For infrastructure companies, the key is whether they can more clearly attribute growth to inference, deployment, and domestic chip compatibility. If task volume expansion continues to outpace the cost reduction from efficiency improvements, computing power, domestic chips, memory, and storage will remain the clearest AI mainline.

title: Iran's Parliament Speaker: Iranian Armed Forces Reorganized During Ceasefire
summary: Iran's Islamic Parliament Speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, met with visiting Pakistani Army Chief General Muhammad Asim Munir on Tuesday. According to Iranian sources, the two sides discussed the latest developments in negotiations. Ghalibaf stated that during the previous ceasefire mediated by Pakistan, the United States 'betrayed' the process by launching a maritime blockade. Additionally, Ghalibaf said that during this temporary ceasefire, the Iranian armed forces underwent reorganization and restructuring. Ghalibaf also warned the United States that if the U.S. government made another mistake and restarted the war, it would face more severe consequences.

title: 3 Trillion Yuan Era: Quantitative Hedge Funds Enter a Survival Competition
summary: Zhejiang Securities noted that the 3 trillion yuan threshold has been crossed, and quantitative hedge funds have officially transitioned from a race to a survival competition. The median excess return of the 500 index enhancement strategies is approaching zero, with the gap between the 90th and 10th percentile managers expanding to 20%. Top institutions are consuming their own excess returns through scale expansion, and the ongoing drawdowns in quantity and price factors have yet to be repaired. Where will the excess returns come from, and why are the drawdowns occurring? These questions have become more critical screening criteria than historical rankings.
content:
The scale of quantitative hedge funds has passed a key threshold. Calculations show that by the end of 2025, the scale of quantitative funds reached 3.22 trillion yuan, accounting for over 43% of private securities investment funds; in 2020, this scale was only 0.76 trillion yuan. The fastest-growing segment is equity quantitative strategies: index enhancement, stock neutrality, and quantitative stock picking account for over 80%.

Chen Olin and colleagues from Zhejiang Securities' financial engineering team pointed out in a report on May 21: "At the 3 trillion yuan scale, the current phase has shifted from a race to a survival competition, and the stability of strategy excess returns may be the core competitiveness of fund managers." The focus is not on the scale itself, but on the changes that follow: excess returns are no longer easily obtainable, and the gaps between fund managers are rapidly widening.

The most striking data comes from the divergence. Under estimated calculations for the first half of 2026, the difference in excess returns between the 90th and 10th percentile managers of private 500 index enhancement products has widened to about 20%, while the gap between the 70th and 30th percentiles is also close to 8%. More importantly, the median is near zero, indicating that a significant portion of products are not outperforming the price index.

Drawdowns have also become harder to explain. Since 2024, the volatility and frequency of excess returns in index enhancement products have increased. By August 2025, low volatility, momentum, small-cap, and liquidity factors all showed significant drag, while the growth factor contributed positive excess returns. It is no longer sufficient to summarize performance differences with just one or two style tags.

The Larger the Scale, the Thinner the Excess

From 2020 to 2025, the total scale of private securities investment funds rose from 4.3 trillion yuan to 7.45 trillion yuan. Quantitative funds were the main source of growth, increasing from 0.76 trillion yuan to 3.22 trillion yuan; non-quantitative funds rose from 3.54 trillion yuan to 4.23 trillion yuan, experiencing years of contraction in between.

Within quantitative strategies, index enhancement remains the largest strategy line, with a scale of about 1.19 trillion yuan at the end of 2025, accounting for nearly 40% of the total quantitative strategy scale. Stock neutrality reached about 0.74 trillion yuan, quantitative stock picking about 0.54 trillion yuan. Quantitative CTA reached 0.37 trillion yuan, while quantitative arbitrage and quantitative options reached 0.11 trillion yuan and 0.03 trillion yuan respectively.

After the scale expansion, pressure on excess returns began to emerge.

From early 2019 to February 2026, the cumulative excess returns of the three major broad-based index enhancement strategies remained upward: 1000 index enhancement about 141%, 500 index enhancement about 109%, and 300 index enhancement about 94%. However, since 2024, the fluctuations have become significantly larger: the 300 index enhancement had negative excess returns in 2024, while the 500 index enhancement experienced continuous drawdowns after July 2025, and the slope of the 1000 index enhancement's excess returns also slowed down.

This change coincided closely with the scale expansion rhythm. From 2020 to 2021, the quantitative scale doubled from 0.76 trillion yuan to 1.46 trillion yuan, and the excess returns of the three major index enhancements fell across the board, with the 1000 index enhancement's excess return dropping from 18.2% to 6.6%. From 2022 to 2023, the scale remained relatively stable, and the excess returns recovered somewhat. In 2024, the scale approached 2 trillion yuan, and the 300 index enhancement's excess return turned negative, while the 500 and 1000 excess returns also dropped to low levels. In 2025, the scale jumped to 3.22 trillion yuan, and the three major index enhancements' excess returns rebounded, but this was largely masked by the extreme small-cap style in the first half of the year.

Advantages of Leading Managers Can Also Be Eaten by Scale

Scale is an enemy of excess returns, and this holds true even for leading managers.

Take H Quantitative as an example. During its explosive performance period from 2019 to 2021, its relative excess return to the same strategy average reached a peak of about 30%. But as the management scale topped out, the excess return narrowed significantly after 2022, returning to near the industry average.

K Investment followed a similar path. During its rapid scale expansion from 2023 to 2024, it still maintained a clear excess return advantage, but after 2025, its relative advantage began to decline, gradually approaching the average of similar strategies; entering 2026, it even showed a slight underperformance compared to the industry average.

This means that the logic of selecting based on top-tier labels is becoming ineffective. The bigger the scale, the harder it is to avoid issues like strategy capacity, trading congestion, and factor decay. Whether a manager can generate excess returns is one thing, and whether they can maintain those returns after expansion is another.

Divergence Is Not Just at the Extremes, the Middle Layer Is Also Beginning to Diverge

In the estimated data for the first half of 2026, the most noteworthy aspect is not the gap between the strongest and weakest, but that the middle layer is also beginning to diverge.

Among private 500 index enhancement products, the difference in excess returns between the 90th and 10th percentiles is approximately 20%, which has approached or even exceeded the extreme level of the same period in 2024. The gap between the 70th and 30th percentiles is about 8%, indicating that the gap is not limited to a few tail-end products but has spread to a broader range.

The median being near zero indicates that the cost of choosing the wrong product has increased. The core selling point of index enhancement products in the past was stable excess returns, but this premise is no longer solid. Simply looking at historical annualized excess returns can misinterpret style dividends as management ability; focusing only on short-term rankings can lead to purchasing drawdowns after style switches.

A more effective question becomes: where do the excess returns come from? When drawdowns occur, is it due to factor failure, or is the portfolio exposure too concentrated? If the latter, the recovery speed usually does not depend solely on market rebounds.

Alpha Sources Are Narrowing, Quantity and Price Factors No Longer Favorable

Behind the performance divergence lies a change in alpha factor structure.

Before 2026, among the four categories of factors—fundamental, analyst expectation, quantity and price, and high-frequency and low-frequency—usually at least three could provide stable positive excess returns. When multiple factors were effective simultaneously, managers using different methodologies could find sources of returns, and thus the performance gaps naturally would not be large.

In recent years, the situation has changed. Those still maintaining positive excess returns are mainly fundamental factors and analyst expectation factors; quantity and price factors, along with high-frequency and low-frequency factors, have been in continuous drawdown since August 2025 and have yet to show a trend toward recovery.

The central tendency of excess returns has also clearly declined. Before the third quarter of 2025, the annualized excess returns of the CSI 500 and CSI 1000 index enhancement strategies were approximately 10% and 13%, respectively; since the third quarter of 2025, the CSI 500 index enhancement has dropped to about 0.75%, and the CSI 1000 index enhancement only about 4.5%.

This directly amplifies differences between fund managers. Combinations with higher proportions of fundamental factors and more balanced factor structures recover from drawdowns faster. For example, Fund Manager Y: with over 30% fundamental factors and about 50% quantity and price factors, the current excess drawdown has recovered to around 0.7%. In contrast, combinations represented by K have tens of thousands of real-time factors, with over 90% being quantity and price factors; when quantity and price factors experienced drawdowns after August 2025, the excess drawdown was greater than the market average and has yet to complete the recovery.

The Main Cause of Drawdowns Is Often Not That the Factors Have Failed

To explain the index enhancement drawdown, simply looking at factor movements is insufficient. A more direct approach is to categorize the stock pool by size and residual volatility: large-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, then overlay high-volatility and low-volatility to form six style domains. This allows the excess drawdown to be split into two parts: deviation of the stock pool, and the factor excess within the stock pool.

Taking the CSI 500 enhancement as an example, the excess drawdown in the drawdown period from August 8 to September 30, 2025, was -4.13%. Within the same period, the low-volatility factor had a drawdown of -8.32%, momentum factor -6.95%, small-cap factor -7.22%, and liquidity factor -5.33%; while the growth factor was +2.60%.

This indicates that the drawdown is not due to all factors failing simultaneously. The directional differences among different factors are significant, and the composition of the portfolio determines how much impact the net value ultimately suffers.

The breakdown of the liquidity factor better illustrates the issue. From August 8 to September 1, 2025, the related portfolio had a drawdown of -3.75%, of which the deviation of the stock pool contributed -3.11%. The deviation within the CSI 500 alone contributed -3.77%, while allocation to other stock pools contributed +0.66%. Looking at the factor excess within the stock pool, the total was -0.70%, while the other stock pools totaled -0.14%.

In other words, this drawdown was primarily not due to the liquidity factor failing severely across all stock domains, but rather the deviation of the portfolio relative to the benchmark dominated the losses, especially the deviation within the benchmark itself.

The Next Round of Screening for Quantitative Hedge Funds Will Be More Rigorous

After reaching 3 trillion yuan, quantitative hedge funds will still be an important force in private securities funds, but the turning point of the industry has changed.

The previous core issue was whether excess returns could be generated, but now there are two additional layers of questions: whether the excess returns rely on a single style, and whether they can be maintained after scale expansion; when drawdowns occur, are they short-term factor disturbances, or has the portfolio structure exposed unmanageable deviations?

This is the meaning of the survival competition. Not all managers will disappear, but under the same index enhancement label, the product curves may be completely different. Excess return stability, risk control capabilities, and factor structure balance will be more important than historical rankings.

It is necessary to retain a boundary: the above returns and drawdowns are calculated based on specific testing periods and samples, and do not represent future results. If the future market data distribution differs from historical patterns, the model may also fail. This article does not constitute a recommendation for fund products, nor does it involve recommendations for any holding stocks.

title: ECB Council Member: Central Bank May Unavoidably Raise Rates to Safeguard Policy Credibility
summary:
Yannis Stournaras, a member of the European Central Bank's Governing Council, said at a European finance ministers' meeting in Nicosia, Cyprus, that safeguarding the ECB's policy credibility is a strong rationale for raising interest rates next month.

"Raising rates comes with costs - for ordinary people and employment alike - which is why I sincerely hope we don't have to get to this point. But if the current impasse continues while we remain inactive, the consequences would be disastrous. For the ECB's credibility and our response mechanism, we may have to raise rates in June," he said.

title: Micron CEO: Memory Shortage May Last Beyond 2026, New Capacity Won't Be Fully Available Until 2028
summary: Recently, Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of US memory chip manufacturer Micron, warned in an interview with foreign media that the current global memory shortage could last beyond 2026, and the industry's true large-scale new capacity release will not be available until at least 2028. "Building the factory infrastructure is currently the longest and most challenging part of the cycle. Even after the civil construction is completed, the equipment installation and commissioning also require a long period," Mehrotra admitted during an interview at his company's Manassas, Virginia plant. The factory has just launched the first DRAM mass production using the '1-alpha' process node in the US, which marks a key step for Micron to bring advanced memory manufacturing back to the domestic market.

content:
On May 23, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province held a press conference to provide details on the gas explosion accident at Lushenyu Coal Mine of Tongzhou Group.
At the meeting, relevant officials stated that the nature of this accident is extremely serious and its impact is extremely negative. We will deeply reflect and remain highly alert, and comprehensively carry out a sweeping inspection in the coal industry.
First, strictly investigate the gas extraction system, focusing on inspecting the extraction equipment and facilities to ensure the integrity of the extraction system, and strictly enforce the principle of 'no extraction, no mining' and 'no production if extraction standards are not met'.
Second, strictly investigate the safety monitoring system, ensuring the system is connected 24 hours a day, data is uploaded in real time, sensors are intact and effective, and it is strictly prohibited to delete monitoring data.
Third, strictly investigate the ventilation system and facilities, ensuring an independent, stable, and reliable ventilation system is established, and it is strictly prohibited to work under conditions of no air flow, weak air flow, or recirculated air flow.
Fourth, conduct a thorough inspection of all underground tunnels, chambers, mined-out areas, coal zones, and old mined-out areas, focusing on verifying whether there are hidden working faces not included in the system, personnel without positioning cards, and areas not covered by monitoring.
Fifth, focus on special inspections in key industries such as hazardous chemicals, non-coal mines, road traffic, and fire safety, and further promote the investigation and rectification of risk hazards.
At 7:29 PM on May 22, a gas explosion occurred at Lushenyu Coal Mine of Tongzhou Group in Qinyuan County, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province, causing major casualties.

title: Extreme Heat as a Structural Economic Risk
summary: Extreme heat is emerging as a structural economic risk: A report by Allianz shows that heatwave events in Europe have increased sevenfold since the 1980s, with the average number of deaths per event rising fivefold. Above the critical threshold of 30°C, every 1°C increase leads to a $1.3 loss in output per hour. If the hottest years of the past decade recur between 2026 and 2030, France could face cumulative GDP losses of $240 billion, Japan $354 billion, and Germany $131 billion. Investment declines by 8%, leading to long-term growth drag. On the fiscal side, France could lose 1.8% in annual tax revenue, while Italy and Spain may again exceed the EU deficit ceiling. Insurance coverage remains insufficient, with only a small portion of the €46 billion in climate-related losses in Europe in 2022 being compensated.

title: China Successfully Develops World's First Silicon-Graphene-Germanium Barrier Transistor for RF Testing, Theoretical Operating Frequency Could Exceed 1 THz
summary: According to the Institute of Metal Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Sun Dongming and Liu Chi's team, in collaboration with multiple research institutions, have achieved a significant breakthrough in high-frequency transistors. The team successfully developed the world's first silicon-graphene-germanium barrier transistor that has been tested for radio frequency applications. The device set a new record for the cutoff frequency of vertical two-dimensional base transistors and achieved the highest current gain value ever recorded for a transistor. The related findings were published on June 6th in the international academic journal Nature Communications. In RF testing, the intrinsic cutoff frequency of the transistor reached 132 GHz, surpassing the previous highest level of all vertical two-dimensional base transistors. Further device modeling and simulation analysis indicate that by optimizing material doping concentration, reducing contact resistance, and minimizing parasitic effects, the theoretical operating frequency of the device could exceed 1 THz, entering the terahertz application band.

title: Regulation and Supervision
summary: Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve, Bowman, testified before the House Committee on Financial Services that the U.S. banking system remains robust with adequate capital and strong liquidity. However, non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) are capturing loan market share at a faster pace and face less regulatory requirements. The Fed has advanced several reforms, including simplifying the community bank leverage ratio framework (set at 8%), modernizing capital rules to promote mortgage lending, and revising the CAMELS rating system. Frontier AI models are accelerating the discovery of network vulnerabilities but also bring new challenges, and the Fed is strengthening public-private collaboration to address them. In the future, the focus will be on adjusting regulatory thresholds, improving the transparency of stress tests, and developing stablecoin rules under the GENIUS Act.

title: From Financial Literacy to Financial Stability
summary: Vice Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank Petar Chobanov emphasized that financial literacy is critical for financial stability. With the rise of digitalization and AI, consumers face new fraud risks, and the central bank has provided tools such as over 200 euro-related Q&A resources and fee comparison websites to promote informed decision-making. Bulgaria joined the eurozone on January 1, 2026, and launched a large-scale public education campaign. Young people should develop savings habits and understand compound interest, while being cautious about behavioral biases and the limitations of AI.

title: Timo Valimaki: The Future of Central Banking and Money - Trust, Resilience, and Innovation
summary: Finland's central bank director Valimäki stated that the future of money depends on trust, resilience, and innovation, with price stability and the anchoring role of central bank currency at its core. Cash transactions in Finland have declined to about 10%, but cash circulation in the eurozone has grown by more than 50% relative to GDP. The digital euro will complement rather than replace private payments, and payment systems need to strengthen resilience as critical infrastructure.

title: Olli Rehn: European Economy Under Pressure from Geopolitical Power Struggles
summary: Finland's central bank governor Olli Rehn stated that the Iran conflict has imposed a stagflationary shock on the European economy, with soaring energy prices undermining growth and pushing up inflation, but medium-term inflation expectations remain anchored near 2%. The central bank may adopt a cautious rate hike, but must avoid overreaction. Meanwhile, he called for Europe to strengthen defense, energy transition, and productivity to address geopolitical challenges.

title: Systemic Risks, Resilience and Competitiveness: Challenges in the Changing Technology Landscape
summary: Finland's central bank governor Rien emphasized at the ESRB meeting that sources of systemic risk have expanded beyond traditional finance, including geopolitical factors, technological disruption and climate risks. AI brings opportunities and challenges, with about one-fifth of Finland's workforce facing the risk of job displacement. Europe needs to simplify regulation, deepen capital market integration, redirect 1.1 trillion euros in deposits toward investment, and strengthen human capital to enhance competitiveness.

title: Zambian Central Bank Governor: The Role of Capital Adequacy and Currency Reform in Financial Stability
summary: The governor of the Bank of Zambia stated that the banking sector's risk exposure to sovereign assets accounts for about one-third of its total assets, highlighting the close link between the sovereign and banks. The central bank revised capital adequacy rules in September 2025, strengthening CET1 and capital buffers; it issued a currency directive in December 2025, limiting dollarization and reinforcing the kwacha's dominance. Preliminary effects have been observed, with several companies shifting to local currency settlements.
Apple announces that Siri AI will be launched on iPadOS. A dedicated Siri AI will be developed for watchOS.

title: Bank of England Expresses Deep Concern Over Forged Posts on X Featuring 'Farage vs. Bailey'
summary: The Bank of England has expressed concerns to Reform UK and related social media platforms over the emergence of numerous posts using fake images that fabricate a scenario in which Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, assaulted Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey. These posts link to a fabricated BBC news article claiming that Farage had a heated confrontation with Bailey on BBC's Question Time program, including fabricated statements and an app link named 'Anocturex'. Bailey stated that fake advertisements impersonating the Bank of England and other central banks are on the rise, aiming to 'criminalize and defraud the public, especially vulnerable groups, online.'

title: Maya McInnis: No State Will Be Immune if Social Security Bankrupts
summary: The U.S. Social Security Trust Fund is projected to be exhausted by 2032, leading to an automatic 24% reduction in benefits, with the average retiree losing $511 per month. Approximately 63 million people nationwide would be affected, resulting in a total loss of $345 billion in benefits, equivalent to 1.1% of the U.S. economy. New York State would be particularly hard-hit, with the cutbacks amounting to 0.8% of its economy.

title: What Investors Should Know About Stock Splits
summary: Stock splits are primarily cosmetic actions that do not alter a company's market value or fundamentals. NVIDIA and Walmart recently executed 10-to-1 and 3-to-1 splits, respectively, aiming to lower stock prices to attract retail investors. Research on the effects of splits is divided: some argue they can enhance liquidity, but there is also evidence suggesting they may harm existing shareholders' interests. Investors should consider splits as part of their investment analysis, not as an independent signal.

title: PPI Index Shows Firms Raising Prices
summary: The PPI trade services index rose 2.7% month-on-month in April, the largest increase since 2010, indicating firms are passing on cost pressures to downstream sectors at the fastest pace. The PPI for final demand increased 6% year-on-year, while core PPI rose 5.2%, both new highs in over three years. The service sector contributed more than half of the increase, with trade services accounting for two-thirds. If May data remains strong, it would confirm the price transmission trend, heightening inflation concerns.

title: 2026 Mid-Year Global Equity Outlook
summary: Charles Schwab released its mid-year 2026 global equity outlook: Strong earnings growth, with MSCI ACWI rising 24% year-on-year in the first quarter, but concentration risk has increased - AI-related companies have contributed most of the growth. Inflation pressures resurface, with Middle East conflicts pushing up PPI, which may soon translate to CPI. Valuations are high, leaving limited room for error. It is recommended to diversify allocations, focusing on earnings quality and opportunities in cyclical stocks.
Apple shares turned lower after initially rising 3.3%.
Apple's stock declined by 1.2%.

Apple is expanding the 'Image Playground' feature, which has seen significant improvements in image generation models, to create 'Contact Posters' and wallpapers. The company also updated the Image Playground API, allowing developers to integrate these new models into their own applications.
Apple CEO Tim Cook said Apple is excited about providing a series of new features to improve people's lives.
Apple executives said: 'I really believe the best is yet to come.'

title: Impact of the World Cup on the U.S. Economy
summary: Goldman Sachs expects the 2026 World Cup to provide a short-term boost to the U.S. economy. During the event, nonfarm payrolls are expected to rise by 40,000 in June and 10,000 in July, but will decline by 15,000 in August. Annualized GDP growth in Q2 and Q3 is expected to gain 0.1 and 0.05 percentage points respectively, primarily driven by retail and service exports fueled by tourist spending. Inflation-wise, core CPI and core PCE are projected to rise by 0.03 and 0.04 percentage points respectively in June, driven by surging hotel and restaurant prices, before gradually reversing.

title: US Labor Market Slack Tracker Updated: Unemployment Rate Expected to Reach Peak of 4.4% This Year
summary: Goldman Sachs updated its labor market slack tracker to 4.8%, indicating the market is weaker than suggested by the unemployment rate but stabilizing. It is expected that the unemployment rate will rise by 0.1 percentage point to a peak of 4.4% this year. Although the average unemployment rate this year is 4.3%, the actual level of slack in the market is higher when considering factors such as job search difficulty.

title: Goldman Sachs Weekly Global Outlook: Stock Market Prospects Amid Rising Rates and Increased Supply
summary: Goldman Raises Treasury Yield Forecasts: Due to strong employment data, Goldman has pushed back its expectation for Federal Reserve rate cuts to 2027, projecting the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield to rise to 4.4% by year-end. Last week, global stocks fell by more than 2%, with U.S. equities leading the decline. Despite record U.S. IPO supply in 2026, demand remains stronger than supply, as the issuance volume accounts for only 1.0% of market cap and buybacks remain robust.

title: Impact of the World Cup on the U.S. Economy
summary:
Main Ideas

  1. Short-term boost in the labor market followed by a decline
    Job gains in June and July are expected to be 40,000 and 10,000 respectively, driven mainly by temporary hiring in the leisure, hospitality, retail, and transportation sectors; however, after the event in August, with the end of temporary positions, employment will decrease by 15,000 and gradually return to trend levels over subsequent months.

  2. GDP growth receives a small seasonal boost
    Driven by foreign tourist spending (counted as service exports) and local resident spending, the annualized GDP growth rate is expected to increase by 0.1 percentage points in the second quarter and 0.05 percentage points in the third quarter; the fourth quarter will face slight drag due to earlier consumption overdrawn.

  3. Inflation data faces temporary upward pressure
    Hotel prices in host cities have already risen sharply, and it is expected that core CPI and core PCE inflation rates will be pushed up by 0.03 and 0.04 percentage points respectively in June; there will be a minor upward impact in July

title: Eurozone Data Update: Germany's Manufacturing Data Mixed; Sentix Survey Remains Weak
summary: Goldman Sachs maintains its Q2 GDP forecast for the Eurozone: Due to a 3.8% decline in Germany's manufacturing orders month-over-month in April (below expectations) but a slight increase in industrial turnover, the Eurozone's Q2 GDP growth forecast remains at 0.16%. sentix survey shows investor assessments of current conditions have further deteriorated to -2.7 standard deviations, while macroeconomic expectations remain stable. New car registration data in France for May remained strong.

title: Hong Kong Real Estate: Beyond Short-Term Volatility
summary: HSBC maintains its 'buy' rating on Hong Kong real estate stocks: Despite short-term fluctuations caused by cross-border fund regulations, the upward trend in the property market remains unchanged, supported by over 280,000 talent inflows and inventory dropping to 11 months. The firm's top picks are Sun Hung Kai Properties, Wharf Holdings, and New World Development, with target prices set at HKD 150.6, HKD 35.8, and HKD 14.4, respectively.

title: Strong Inflows but Away from Long End: Analysis of U.S. Interest Rate Fund Flows
summary: Barclays research shows strong inflows into U.S. bond funds with structural divergence. As of the week ending June 4, bond funds saw 19.1 billion dollars in inflows, with a cumulative total of 28.2 billion dollars since the start of the year. Funds were concentrated in short- to medium-term instruments, with demand for short-term corporate bonds at a 97% high percentile. In contrast, long-end Treasury demand remained weak, with long-term government funds continuing to experience outflows. Meanwhile, money market funds surged by 10.9 billion dollars in a single week, pushing total assets to a record high. Foreign investor demand softened, with Japanese investors net selling, and the Federal Reserve's custodial account holdings of U.S. Treasuries declined by 3.27 billion dollars for the week.

title: U.S. Labor Market Slack Tracker Update: Unemployment Rate Expected to Reach Peak of 4.4% This Year
summary:
Main Ideas

  1. Signs of Stability in the Labor Market, but Slack Indicators Suggest a Weaker Market Than Unemployment Rates Imply
    Although the unemployment rate averaged 4.3% this year and potential employment growth reached or exceeded the breakeven level, indicators such as those from the Conference Board that measure job search difficulty suggest an increase in labor market slack. The updated Goldman Sachs Slack Tracker indicates that the actual state of the labor market is more relaxed than what a single unemployment rate suggests, though recent data show signs of stability.

  2. Unemployment Rate Expected to Rise by 0.1 Percentage Point This Year, Peaking at 4.4%
    Considering strong employment growth alongside weaker signals from the Slack Tracker, Goldman Sachs forecasts the unemployment rate will rise by only 0.1 percentage point this year, reaching a peak of 4.4%. This forecast balances mixed signals from different data sources.

    Goldman Sachs has updated its Slack Tracker, which it has

title: Barclays Global Macro View: Strong US Labor Market, Fed Holds Steady, Risk Assets Expected to Rise After Short-Term Volatility
summary: Barclays: Strengthening US Labor Market, High Bar for 2026 Rate Hikes. US 3mma new jobs added 188,000, with wage growth below 4%. The Federal Reserve is expected to hold steady, while the ECB will raise rates. Risk assets are expected to experience short-term volatility but remain bullish in the medium term; short-duration US Treasuries are viewed as overvalued. The 5y5y SOFR reached 4.3%, with insufficient term premium.

title: Midstream: Too Much Good News (IV) - This Will End
summary: Barclays research notes that the natural gas export market in the Permian Basin will ease after Q3 2026, but will tighten again in the first half of 2028, with current futures pricing overly optimistic. It recommends producers to increase basis hedging in 2028. APA Corp, which has excess fixed transportation capacity, is expected to generate $1.1 billion in pre-tax cash flow in 2026, making it the biggest beneficiary; Energy Transfer is likely to benefit from contract revenue streams; while ONEOK and Kinder Morgan may face negative impacts due to narrowing basis spreads.

title: BDCs and REITs: Lessons from Past Redemption Waves
summary: Barclays research indicates that private perpetual BDCs are facing redemption pressures similar to those seen in non-traded REITs during 2022-2024, with expected deterioration in net outflows in 2Q26. BCRED's redemption requests in 2Q26 reached 10% (capped at 5%). The report emphasizes asset quality and institutional support as key differentiators, advising investors to focus on BDCs with lower software exposure and GP support. Blackstone (BX) received an upgrade rating following its success in stabilizing BREIT, with a price target of $124.

summary: Barclays analyzes the Bain report: Private equity deals slowed in 2026, technology transactions dropped by 70% quarter-over-quarter, and software valuations fell by 8%. title: Hong Kong Real Estate: Another Wave of Challenges
summary: JPMorgan noted that Hong Kong property stocks are under short-term pressure due to mainland capital controls and concerns over interest rate hikes, but maintains its forecast of a 10-15% increase in housing prices in 2026. It recommends investors to take advantage of lower prices to buy high-quality stocks such as Sun Hung Kai Properties and Hin Leung Property, while avoiding developers with high leverage.

title: G10 FX Strategy: Investors Increase Dollar Long Positions After Strong Nonfarm Payrolls Data
summary: Morgan Stanley reports that due to stronger-than-expected nonfarm payrolls data, investors have recently increased dollar long positions and New Zealand dollar short positions. However, industrial turnover increased by 0.1% month-on-month in April, better than the initial estimate of -0.9%, although lower than March's reported +1.2%. Overall, these data point to a 0.4% month-on-month increase in industrial production in April.

  3. Investor Sentiment Index Shows Further Deterioration in Current Assessments
    The June early Sentix investor survey showed that the current assessment component deteriorated further by 0.2 standard deviations to -2.7 standard deviations, while the macroeconomic expectations component remained larg

title: Morgan Stanley: Macro Strategy Outlook Amid Strong Nonfarm Payrolls and Slowing Inflation
summary: Morgan Stanley noted that the three-month average of nonfarm payrolls rose to 188,000, indicating a strong labor market and reducing concerns at the Federal Reserve. The core CPI increased by 0.22% on a month-over-month basis, showing a slowdown in inflation. As long as the Federal Reserve does not raise interest rates, S&P 500 stocks, especially cyclical stocks, remain attractive, with historical data showing an average return of 16.3% in such environments. However, caution is needed regarding volatility risks if the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield exceeds 4.5%. The firm maintains a constructive view on U.S. equities and expects a decline in Treasury yields.

title: Morgan Stanley Foresees Bank of Japan's June Policy Meeting: Expected Rate Hike to 1.0%, Yen Likely to Remain in Range
summary: Morgan Stanley expects the Bank of Japan to raise rates to 1.0% in June: Unless the situation in the Middle East deteriorates, the central bank is likely to pass the rate hike with an 8-1 majority vote, with the market pricing in a probability of over 90%. It is expected that the monthly purchase of 2.1 trillion yen in government bonds will be maintained starting April 2027. Due to the market's perception that the Bank of Japan remains behind the curve and faces intervention risks, the USD/JPY exchange rate is expected to remain in a range-bound pattern, with limited impact on the foreign exchange market from the rate hike.

title: Does Outperforming US Equities Necessarily Lead to a Stronger Dollar? The Answer Lies in the Bond Market
summary: Morgan Stanley notes that outperforming US equities does not necessarily lead to a stronger dollar, with the key factor being changes in the US Treasury yield spread. If US equities outperform but the spread narrows, the dollar will weaken; if the spread expands in tandem, the dollar will only see a modest increase. Historical data shows that for every 1% outperformance of the S&P 500, the DXY fell by 16 basis points. The firm maintains its view that the June FOMC meeting remains a key turning point for the dollar's movement.

title: North American Trade Weekly Report: From Rules to Discretion, from Automobiles to Artificial Intelligence
summary: Morgan Stanley notes that North American trade is undergoing structural reshaping, with U.S. policy shifting toward discretion and import demand concentrating on AI-related goods. Mexico benefits from nearshoring and supply chain integration with the U.S., outperforming Canada in export performance. It is expected that inflation driven by tariffs will ease in the second half of 2026, supporting disinflation and enabling the Fed to maintain accommodative policies through 2027, but policy upside risks should be monitored.

title: Weekly Preview: A Healthy Reset
summary: Morgan Stanley maintains its year-end target of 8,000 for the S&P 500, viewing Friday's semiconductor sector decline as a healthy reset. Despite the SOX index falling 10% in a single day, the breadth of earnings revisions reached a cycle high of 26%, and the ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 54. The firm recommends focusing on discretionary consumption, transportation, and regional banks, as short-term liquidity tightening is supported by strong fundamentals that sustain the bull market.

title: Semiconductor Equipment: Survey Notes from Japan and Taiwan
summary: Morgan Stanley released a survey note on semiconductor equipment, reiterating the expansion of DRAM demand, and expecting Vera CPU to account for over 10% of global DRAM bit demand in 2025. The institution upgraded Advantest (6857.T) to preferred stock, highlighting its advantages in CPO testing and AI GPU sectors, with the CPO testing market potentially reaching $300 million to $700 million by 2028. A shortage of memory is expected to persist for 2-3 years, benefiting front-end wafer process manufacturers.

    Although investor sentiment may remain weak due to sensitivity to capital flows, leading to a 12.5% decline in developers' stock prices since May 22, outperforming the Hang Seng Index by 8.7 percentage points, HSBC maintains a constructive view on the property market outlook. Supporting factors include net population growth, depletion of private housing supply, and positive holding cost advantages.

    Since the introduction of various talent attraction programs at the end of 2022, over 280,000 people have moved to Hong Kong for work, a number equivalent to 12.6 times the first-hand sales volume in 2025. On the supply side, the inventory months dropped from 23 months in Q1 2024 to 11 months in Q1 2026, and unsold completed inventory fell below 20,000 units, indicating a significant improvement in supply and demand dynamics.

summary: Goldman Sachs maintains its "buy" rating on Eli Lilly (LLY) with a price target of $1,283. title: UBS Global Macro Chart of the Day: Lessons from the 2022 Energy Crisis on GDP Impact
summary: UBS noted that energy consumption in the eurozone fell by 21% in 2022, but GDP showed little contraction, primarily due to production shifting toward low-energy sectors. German chemical industry reduced output by 2.9%, saving gas consumption, while the automotive sector increased output by 17%, with only a 0.5pp increase in gas usage. summary: JPMorgan hosted its 2026 Quantitative and AI Conference, bringing together 520 institutions to discuss industry transformation. Experts emphasized that while AI enhances efficiency, robust research processes and out-of-sample performance remain critical for quantitative success, which is expected to drive a productivity boom in the strategy domain.

Most of the risk exposure has already been managed, and only the remaining risk exposure could affect profits. "As silver prices decline, the company will also strategically stock a portion of inventory, but the overall scale is small, as silver is a precious metal and holding more inventory requires significant capital," Fuda Alloy said.

title: Youjia Innovation Secures Over 130 Million Yuan in Orders for L4 Autonomous Buses
summary: Youjia Innovation announced that it has recently signed an 'Autonomous Vehicle Procurement Contract' with an independent third party specializing in smart transportation. Under the agreement, Youjia Innovation will supply autonomous buses, self-driving kits, and related technical services to the partner. The contract involves hundreds of autonomous buses and associated services, with a total amount including tax exceeding 130 million yuan. The delivered products will primarily be applied in local cultural tourism, micro-circulation, and public transportation scenarios.

title: Israeli military reports killing of cross-border armed personnel in northern region
summary: The Israeli military stated that Israeli forces were "shot at" today (June 9) in the Ramim Ridge area in northern Galilee. The military returned fire and killed one "cross-border armed individual." The Israeli military said the incident is still ongoing. According to Israeli media reports, residents in multiple communities near the temporary Israel-Lebanon border in northern Israel received emergency instructions to "take immediate shelter on-site." Emergency traffic control has been implemented in the area, with some road sections closed.

title: China's Central Bank Holds Fourth China-Brazil Financial Strategic Cooperation Working Group Meeting
summary: The fourth China-Brazil Financial Strategic Cooperation Working Group meeting was held, with Governor Pan Gongsheng of the People's Bank of China and Governor Galipolo of the Central Bank of Brazil jointly presiding over the meeting.

title: China-South Korea Semiconductor ETF HuaTai Boli Rises to Limit, Issues Premium Risk Warnings Over 170 Times This Year
summary: Today, the China-South Korea Semiconductor ETF HuaTai Boli surged to the daily limit. The ETF tracks the China Securities Index South Korean Exchange China-South Korea Semiconductor Index, which consists of major South Korean semiconductor companies (such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix) and leading A-share semiconductor firms (such as SMIC and GigaDevice). Notably, the premium rate of the China-South Korea Semiconductor ETF HuaTai Boli has reached as high as 19.36%, and it has issued premium risk warnings over 170 times this year.

title: Hong Kong International Airport Launches 'Yibo You' Service in July
summary: Starting today (June 9), the 'Yue Vehicle Southbound' policy has added five Guangdong cities - Shenzhen, Dongguan, Huizhou, Foshan, and Zhaoqing. The Hong Kong Airport Authority stated that travelers from these cities can apply for the 'Yibo Fei' service at Hong Kong International Airport. After approval, they can drive through the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge to the airport's automated parking lot starting June 15, park their vehicles, and then proceed to the airport restricted area to board flights.

title: China Jinmao: May Contracted Sales Reach 10.49 Billion Yuan
summary: China Jinmao announced on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange that in May 2026, the group achieved contracted sales of 1.0493 billion yuan, with a contracted sales area of 368,427.48 square meters.

title: Predictive market traders: Strait of Hormuz shipping likely to remain disrupted in 2026
summary: Iran's chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Ali Larijani stated on June 8 that Iran will turn the U.S. maritime blockade into another failure for its adversaries. More than 100 days have passed since the conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran began, with the struggle over passage through the Strait of Hormuz and the blockade of Iran's imports and exports becoming increasingly prolonged. According to a report by CNBC on June 8, predictive market traders indicated that it is highly unlikely that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will return to normal by 2026. On predictive market platforms, the probability of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz resuming normal operations before January 2027 stands at 65.5%, while the probability of it resuming normal operations before August this year has dropped from over 60% to 21.5% in the past two weeks.

title: Luckin Coffee's Tea Drinks Sold 20 Billion Yuan, the Boundary of Fresh Beverage Categories Begins to Disappear
summary: The boundaries between coffee shops, tea shops, and fruit tea stores are becoming increasingly blurred. Tea brands are starting to sell Americanos and lattes, while coffee brands are introducing fruit teas, light milk teas, and yogurt smoothies. Baked goods, desserts, ready-to-drink beverages, and fresh beverages are also beginning to overlap. As of May 31, 2026, the total sales of fresh tea drinks and other non-coffee beverages at Luckin's nationwide stores exceeded 20 billion yuan. This figure includes sales of tea drinks and other non-coffee beverages, and represents the cumulative total since Luckin's establishment. (According to market sources)
Gongjin Securities plans to repurchase shares with a total amount ranging from 150 million to 300 million yuan, with the repurchase price not exceeding 13 yuan per share.

title: BASF Warns of Potential Automotive Supply Chain Disruptions from Iran Conflict
summary: The CEO of chemical giant BASF said that rising inflation and the risk of supply chain disruptions due to the Iran conflict are casting a shadow over the automotive industry and overall economic outlook. He noted that the possibility of raw material shortages is increasing, which could lead to stagnation in highly sophisticated supply chains such as automobile production. He added that the conflict has already caused shortages of inputs such as sulfur and helium.

title: General Administration of Customs Announces Regulations on the Declaration of Drone-Related Items for Export
summary: Announcement No. 78 of 2026 by the General Administration of Customs (Notice on the Regulation of the Declaration of Drones and Related Items for Export). It states that the term 'drones and related items' refers to unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned airships and their associated equipment and components, and civil anti-unmanned aerial vehicle systems, among others.
Apple introduces AI-powered experiences across multiple services.
Broadcom pre-market shares rose as much as 3% as Broadcom, Apollo and Blackstone Group established a strategic platform to accelerate global AI deployment exceeding 20 gigawatts.

summary: Chinese automakers are beginning to enter its factories.
Wells Fargo: Japan is unlikely to intervene in the yen exchange rate before the central bank's policy meeting.

title: Cash shortages hit ATMs in Indian cities, with some second- and third-tier cities unable to dispense cash
summary: According to financial media reports on June 8, ATMs in several second- and third-tier cities in India have recently faced a 'cash shortage,' causing difficulties for local residents in withdrawing cash. The Indian ATM Industry Association said the main reason for this situation is that major banks are prioritizing the allocation of cash to big cities. Industry data shows that the cash demand for ATMs across India was 940 billion rupees in March and April this year, while the actual supply was 610 billion rupees and 540 billion rupees respectively.

title: Lanxess CEO: China Has Adequate Oil and Gas Reserves, Local Plants Operate Smoothly
summary: Despite the sharp increase in global chemical raw material prices due to the Middle East conflict, Lanxess's plant in Ningbo, Zhejiang has continued to operate normally," said Matthias Zachert, CEO and Chairman of the Management Board of the German specialty chemicals company Lanxess, recently. "China has done a very good job in its strategy, with sufficient oil and gas reserves." While companies in several Asian countries have been forced to issue force majeure notices due to supply chain disruptions, Lanxess's plants in China have remained smoothly operational.

title: Suzhou Liansheng Receives Inquiry from Shanghai Stock Exchange: Feasibility of Building a 120,000-Plate Per Year 4-6 Inch Indium Phosphide Substrate Production Line Within 10 Months
summary: The Shanghai Stock Exchange has issued an inquiry to Suzhou Liansheng. Previously, Suzhou Liansheng announced that it plans to sign a cooperation intention agreement with individual shareholder Zhu Ronghui and Hui Zhi Guangxin Artificial Intelligence Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. The company intends to jointly invest 10 million yuan to establish a joint venture for the research and production and sales of indium phosphide substrates, with the company contributing 7 million yuan, accounting for 70% equity. Subsequently, each shareholder will invest a total of 300 million yuan in two phases based on their shareholding ratio, used for the construction of the indium phosphide substrate project.

title: Why is the First Disruptive Industry in the Space Economy Medicine?
summary: The space economy is moving from concept to commercialization, with the pharmaceutical industry being the first high-value application validated. The microgravity environment significantly improves drug crystal quality, driving innovations in drug delivery methods and production processes. Merck's experimental verification and the involvement of major players like Eli Lilly have moved space-based pharmaceuticals from research to industrialization, becoming a key breakthrough for the commercial value of the space economy.

summary: Nasdaq rises 0.7%, S&P 500 index gains 0.44%, and Dow Jones rises 0.06%. title: IATA Warns Global Airlines' Profits Could Be Halved Due to $100 Billion Surge in Fuel Costs
summary: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) warned that rising fuel costs are squeezing the industry's viability, and global airlines' profits are expected to drop by half in 2026. The organization stated that the soaring fuel costs will lead to a collective increase of $100 billion in fuel bills for global airlines.

title: Executive of Longi Green Energy: Energy Storage Business Will Not Rush to Expand Scale, Avoids Repeating Past Mistakes in PV Industry
summary: ``Longi will not blindly pursue scale from the beginning in energy storage, the core is to create best-selling products.' said She Haifeng, vice president of Longi Green Energy and head of its energy storage business, during the recent SNEC, the world's largest photovoltaic and energy storage exhibition. The company's strategy for its energy storage business differs from earlier entrants in the PV industry, and it will not repeat the pitfalls of 'homogenized competition' in the PV sector.
India reportedly freezes the approval of Starlink's project citing security concerns.

title: Perplexity CEO: Company Plans 2028 IPO Regardless of Anthropic or OpenAI's Listing Progress
summary: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas stated that the AI company plans to go public in 2028. This statement comes as Anthropic has secretly filed for an IPO, while investors are assessing the performance of SpaceX, which is set to list soon. Srinivas said he believes the IPOs of Anthropic and the rumored listing of OpenAI will receive strong market reactions. 'We maintain a neutral stance toward both companies, and our original plan to take action in 2028 remains valid,' he said. Srinivas had previously indicated that the company had no immediate plans to go public before 2028. His latest remarks further clarify the timeline for the IPO.

title: Satellogic Surges 270% This Year as Global Space Sector Heats Up
summary: Satellogic's stock has surged over 270% this year, emerging as one of the biggest winners in the 2026 space sector boom. The company has successfully transitioned to low-cost satellite manufacturing and government-grade Earth observation services, tapping into sovereign and defense demand and achieving positive operating cash flow for the first time. With the upcoming deployment of its 'Merlin' constellation and rising demand driven by geopolitical tensions, its profit path is becoming clearer, but high valuations and long-term government contracts still pose uncertainties.

title: Kalshi Traders Say Hormuz Strait Shipping Will Struggle to Return to Normal Before January
summary: On the prediction market platform Kalshi, the probability of Hormuz Strait resuming normal shipping before January has risen to 66%. In the past two weeks, the probability of the strait resuming normal shipping before August has dropped sharply from 66% to 21%. title: Rivian Bets on R2 Electric Vehicle to Build a Household Name Brand, Competing with Tesla
summary: On June 9, 'Tesla rival' Rivian officially launched the R2 electric vehicle, with customer deliveries starting. Meanwhile, the company pushed forward the release of its $45,000 entry-level model from late 2027 to next summer. The launch of the R2 SUV aims to transform Rivian from a niche electric vehicle manufacturer selling luxury models into a mainstream brand like Tesla, the leader in the U.S. electric vehicle market. Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe stated that he believes the R2 will not only compete with Tesla but also challenge traditional mainstream automotive brands such as Jeep and Subaru.
ASML shares climbed 4.5%, marking the first time its market capitalization exceeded $70 billion.
WTI crude oil fell 4.0% on the day, trading at $87.54 per barrel; Brent crude oil dropped 3.5% on the day, reaching $90.86 per barrel.

title: Emerging Chip Maker Continues to Challenge Nvidia, This Time with Microsoft-backed D-Matrix
summary:
D-Matrix, a startup that has entered mass production, claims its chip runs inference workloads 10 times faster than the market leader Nvidia's standalone GPU when the workload is small, and consumes only one-fifth the power. The new inference chip, named Corsair, uses a novel approach to memory processing, similar to Cerebras and Groq.

"This is a trillion-dollar market forming," said Sid Sheth, co-founder and CEO of D-Matrix, who has no intention of selling the company. "The market can absolutely support another publicly traded company."
JPMorgan is set to deploy more powerful AI agents this year.

title: Shengquan Group: Advanced Electronic Materials Prices Remain Stable, No Significant Price Hike Reported
summary: Regarding the question of whether the company's electronic-grade resin products have experienced price increases against the backdrop of global PPE resin supply disruptions, Shengquan Group responded on its interactive platform that the high molecular weight polyphenylene ether (PPE) mentioned in media reports, which is being mass-produced in the Jubail Industrial Area of Saudi Arabia, belongs to the engineering plastics category. The product focuses on mechanical strength, heat resistance, and dimensional stability, with downstream applications in the automotive, home appliance, and industrial equipment sectors. The company's electronic-grade PPO resin focuses on low dielectric, low loss, and high-speed signal transmission characteristics, primarily used in copper-clad laminate (CCL) applications. The two belong to different product systems, with significant differences in technical routes and end markets, and there is no business relationship between them. Recently, the prices of the company's advanced electronic materials have remained stable, with no significant price increases reported.

title: HKEX Announces Major Adjustment: Price Limits for After-Hours Trading (T+1 Period) Expanded to ±6%
summary: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited released a notice titled 'Optimization Measures for After-Hours Trading (T+10 Period)', stating that it will further optimize the price limits for specified stock index futures contracts during the after-hours trading (T+1) period, expanding the current limit of ±5% to ±6%. The contracts include the Hang Seng Index Futures, Hang Seng Index Dividend Accumulation Index Futures, Hang Seng China Enterprises Index Futures, Hang Seng China Enterprises Index Dividend Accumulation Index Futures, Hang Seng Tech Index Futures, Small Hang Seng Index Futures, and Small Hang Seng China Enterprises Index Futures, but exclude the Hang Seng Biotechnology Index Futures.

title: Wuhan Iron and Steel Group Appoints New General Manager
summary:
According to a notice from the official WeChat account 'Happy Wuhan Iron and Steel', on June 9, Wuhan Iron and Steel Group held a meeting to announce personnel adjustments. China Baowu Steel Group adjusted the leadership of Wuhan Iron and Steel Group. Li Lina, member of the Party Committee and Chief Financial Officer of China Baowu Steel Group, attended the meeting and delivered a speech. Xiao Yang, secretary of the Party Committee, chairman, and general representative of Wuhan headquarters of China Baowu Steel Group, presided over the meeting. At the meeting, a relevant official from the Organization Department of the Party Committee of China Baowu Steel Group announced the personnel adjustment decision regarding Wuhan Iron and Steel Group.

After research by the Standing Committee of the Party Committee of China Baowu Steel Group, Fan Hongchao was appointed as the general manager of Wuhan Iron and Steel Group, and will continue to serve as a director of Wuhan Iron and Steel Group and deputy secretary of the Party Committee. The appointment of the position will be processed according to relevant regulations and procedures.
Nasdaq turned lower, while S&P 500 maintained a gain of more than 0.2%, and the semiconductor index fell 0.2%.

title: Thailand's Former Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra Granted Pardon
summary: According to market sources, Thailand's former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra has had his electronic monitoring device removed and has been granted a pardon. Previously, the Thai Minister of Justice Rutapong said in an interview that according to a royal pardon issued by King Maha Vajiralongkorn, former prime minister Thaksin meets the conditions for pardon and is one of the individuals who will be pardoned.
U.S. Energy Secretary Wright said oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf are expected to rise.

Data center developer Crusoe has paused its AI project in Wyoming, USA. The company announced that it has secured 4.9 GW of AI capacity. Previously, the company had partnered with Tallgrass, backed by Blackstone Group, in Wyoming.
Silver on the spot market fell 3.0% to $66.1 per ounce. New York silver dropped 3.5% to $66.13 per ounce.

title: Survey: Economists Expect Federal Reserve to Hold Rates in 2026 Amid Persistent Inflation from Conflicts
summary: Latest survey results show that about 70% (72 out of 102) of economists surveyed expect the benchmark interest rate to remain within the current range of 3.50%-3.75% for the rest of 2026, a proportion higher than less than half last month and about one-third previously. The survey was conducted from June 4 to June 9. No economist predicted that the Federal Reserve would cut rates after the FOMC meeting on June 16-17. This marks the first clear consensus this year that inflation driven by conflicts is more persistent than expected.

U.S. major stock indices turned lower, with the S&P falling about 0.5%, the Nasdaq dropping 267 points, a decline of over 1%, the Nasdaq Composite index down 1.2%, and the semiconductor index slipping 2.6%.

title: CFTC Abandons New Headquarters Relocation Plan Amid Market Growth Outlook
summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) announced it will abandon its planned headquarters relocation and instead extend its current lease for five years. The agency cited the need for more spacious office space in the future as the reason. The regulatory body plans to expand its workforce. A spokesperson stated that remaining in the current office building will provide sufficient space for the agency to hire more new employees. Meanwhile, the CFTC has offered a 'buyout' or early retirement program to approximately 50 employees, which will affect many positions in the market supervision division, particularly those of analysts and economists.

title: Nantong Unveils Three-Year Plan to Integrate AI with Energy
summary: Recently, the Nantong Development and Reform Commission issued the 'Three-Year Action Plan for Accelerating the Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Energy in Nantong.' The plan also released a list of 31 typical application scenarios under development, construction, and planning in the field of 'Artificial Intelligence + Energy,' covering key areas such as smart grids, new energy maintenance, emerging energy industries, intelligent operation of thermal power plants, and oil and gas safety management. The plan proposes that by 2028, two or so specialized large models in vertical fields will be deeply applied in the energy industry, cultivating more than 10 competitive, scalable, and replicable practice cases and typical application scenarios, forming a new model of artificial intelligence innovation and development in the energy sector with Nantong characteristics.

title: Venezuela and Energy Giant IMPSA Advance Key Hydroelectric Contract Restructuring to Avert Grid Collapse
summary: Energy giant IMPSA is renegotiating a landmark hydroelectric contract that has been stalled for over a decade with the Venezuelan government, which is expected to inject up to 672 megawatts (MW) of much-needed power generation capacity into Venezuela's struggling national grid in the coming months. Meta will use its shared data business to fine-tune advertising. The company stated that this upgrade does not include any new data collection from users.

title: India Weighs Extending Duty-Free Import Period for Petrochemical Products Beyond June 30
summary:
Ravi Teja, Deputy Secretary of India's Ministry of Commerce, stated that India is considering extending the duty-free import policy for petrochemical products used in plastic manufacturing and pharmaceuticals beyond June 30 to support domestic industries. 'The Ministry is closely monitoring developments. The final decision on whether to extend the duty exemption must be made after a comprehensive assessment of the current geopolitical situation, provided that the ministry deems it necessary,' he said.

In April, the Indian government announced a suspension of import duties on 40 types of petrochemical products, which were originally set to expire on June 30. The measure aims to help various sectors address the nationwide shortage of medicines and raw materials caused by the outbreak of the Iran conflict (Reuters).
LPG futures closed down about 4% on the night session, fuel oil fell more than 2.9%, and low sulfur fuel oil dropped more than 2.6%.
Boeing delivered 51 737 Max aircraft and 6 787 aircraft.

title: Hamas Spokesperson: Reached 'Acceptable Solutions' on Multiple Issues in Ceasefire Agreement
summary: A spokesperson for the Palestinian Islamic Resistance Movement (Hamas), Hazem Qassem, stated in a statement that Palestinian factions and mediators reached 'acceptable solutions' on multiple difficult issues in the ceasefire agreement during the latest round of talks held in Cairo. Qassem said whether the ceasefire agreement can smoothly transition to its second phase depends on whether mediators, guarantor countries, and the 'Peace Committee' can effectively constrain Israel to stop violating the terms and accept the current solutions and consensus.
Prosus repurchased 2.631597 million shares at an average price of 40.7439 euros during the week ending June 5, totaling over 107.2 million euros (equivalent to more than 124.5 million USD).

title: PetroChina Appoints Dai Houliang as Chairman
summary: PetroChina announced that the board of directors elected Dai Houliang as chairman of the company, Zhou Xinhuai as vice chairman, and approved the appointment of Ren Lixin as president of the company. It also appointed Zhang Daowei and Song Dayong as senior vice presidents, and Yang Weisheng, Yang Liqiang, Dai Qiongrong, and Wang Guofeng as vice presidents. Additionally, Wang Hua was appointed as the company's secretary of the board and chief financial officer.

title: Canada's Trade Surplus Rises to Record High in April Amid Export Surge
summary:
Driven by a strong performance across all exports, Canada's goods trade surplus surged to CAD 2.72 billion in April, significantly higher than CAD 1.75 billion in March. This marks the second consecutive month of a trade surplus for Canada and represents the highest surplus since January 2026.

Total exports in April rose 1.6% month-over-month to a record CAD 75.2 billion. Energy exports played a key role, with crude oil exports jumping 7% amid rising oil prices.

Canada's monthly trade surplus with the United States, its largest trading partner, reached its highest level since February 2025—before the first round of tariffs imposed by former U.S. President Donald Trump on Canadian imports. This was mainly driven by strong exports of crude oil, passenger vehicles, and light trucks to the U.S., which increased 4.8% to CAD 9.5 billion.
According to market sources, SpaceX's IPO in the US has attracted multiple times oversubscription.
The EU has ordered Meta to suspend restrictions on AI competitors for WhatsApp, requiring the company to comply within five business days.
S&P 500 index declines by 1%.
